questions.question: How many distinct real roots does the biquadratic equation $x^4 - 13x^2 + 42 = 0$ analyzed in Mathematical Reasoning & Linear Programming (Boolean Algebra Duality) possess?
questions.solution: Factoring $(x^2 - 6)(x^2 - 7) = 0$ with $6 \neq 7 > 0$ yields $4$ distinct real roots $\pm\sqrt{6}, \pm\sqrt{7}$.

questions.question: If the equations $x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0$ and $x^2 - 9x + k = 0$ in Mathematical Reasoning & Linear Programming (Tautology & Contrapositive Logic) share the common root $x = 1$, find the value of $k$.
questions.solution: Substituting the common root $x = 1$ into the second equation gives $1 - (9) + k = 0 \implies k = 8$.
questions.explanation: Apply common roots & parameter elimination techniques in Mathematical Reasoning & Linear Programming (Tautology & Contrapositive Logic).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Two quadratic equations $2x^2 + 16x + 18 = 0$ and $x^2 + p x + q = 0$ in Mathematical Reasoning & Linear Programming (Corner Point Feasible Region) have both roots in common. Find $p + q$.
questions.solution: Proportionality of coefficients $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{p}{16} = \frac{q}{18} \implies p = 8,\; q = 9 \implies p + q = 17$.
questions.explanation: Apply common roots & parameter elimination techniques in Mathematical Reasoning & Linear Programming (Corner Point Feasible Region).

questions.question: In Mathematical Reasoning & Linear Programming (Negation of Quantified Statements), find the largest integral value of parameter $m$ for which the number $x = 3$ lies strictly between the roots of $f(x) = x^2 - 6x + m = 0$.
questions.solution: For $x = 3$ to lie strictly between the roots, $f(3) < 0 \implies 3^2 - 2(3^2) + m < 0 \implies m < 9$, so largest integer is $8$.
questions.explanation: Apply location of roots on real axis techniques in Mathematical Reasoning & Linear Programming (Negation of Quantified Statements).
